headline: Cancel paired values with XOR
statement: Every value in nums occurs exactly twice except one value occurring once. Return that unique value using linear time and constant extra space.
constraints: Exactly one value occurs once; all others occur twice.
intuition: The XOR operation cancels two equal numbers: x XOR x is zero. Apply XOR to every input value. All the pairs cancel, leaving only the number that appears once. The order does not matter, so no sorting or count table is needed.
correctness: After any prefix, result is its XOR. For the full array, associativity and commutativity allow identical values to be grouped; each pair becomes zero. The sole unpaired value remains, including when it is negative.
bruteForce: Count occurrences with a dictionary in O(n) space, then return the count-one key. XOR uses the promised occurrence counts to remove that storage.

complexity.explanation: One accumulator processes every value once.

pitfalls: This relies on exactly two copies of every paired value.
XOR is ^ in Python, not exponentiation **.
Do not use sum cancellation: paired values do not add to zero.
